newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai rice output to post steady growth - official.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice output to post steady growth - official.

text.p: Thai rice production is projected to grow slowly to 21.01 million tonnes in 2001 against 20.43 million tonnes in 1997, two experts from Bangkok's Agriculture Department said on Thursday.

Boriboon Somrith and Ngamchuen Kongseree, rice experts with the Thai Agriculture office, told delegates at the Asia rice conference in Singapore that hectarage planted to rice will drop to 9.26 million hectares in 2001 compared with 9.33 million hectares in 1997.
But yield per hectare should rise to 2.27 tonnes against 2.19 tonnes in 1997, the two officials said.
Serious flood damage in the lower north and central plains of Thailand will lead to a fall in production this year to 17.7 million tonnes.
"Thai farmers are in need of new rice varieties with multiple resistance, combined with high grain quality," Boriboon and Ngamchuen said in their report.
Disease and insects are the main barriers to higher yields on Thai farms, they said.
